issue_context.title: Defaults aren't applied to duplicated profile until saved
issue_context.body:
### Windows Terminal version (or Windows build number)

main 6657d2c

### Other Software

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set your default font size to 9.
2. Make a duplicate of the "PowerShell" profile.

### Expected Behavior

The font size for the duplicated profile should display as 9.

### Actual Behavior

The font size for the duplicated profile is shown as 12. Clicking save updates the profile and the default font size is applied.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5821575/135661487-61af3bf8-cde4-4eb1-a5e2-fed0768c6bbf.mp4

This is _not_ a problem in stable (1.10.2383.0).
comments: I also can't repro this in preview (1.11.2731.0), so this is a 1.12 regression.
This might not make it in time for the 1.12 cut, but we should probably service it back to 1.12
@zadjii-msft Can you please try to reproduce this bug? I can't reproduce it on neither 1.12.2781.0, nor c727762.

@ianjoneill quick question, did you _save_ the settings before making the duplicate?

If I:

1. Set your default font size to 9.
2. Save the settings
2. Make a duplicate of the "PowerShell" profile.

Then the duplicate will have the font size set to 9.

However, if I only:
1. Set your default font size to 9.
2. Make a duplicate of the "PowerShell" profile.

Then the duplicate inherits the original "defaults" value, not the (unsaved) one. This seems to make sense to me?

That doesn't make sense to me. The duplicate should be a new child of the `defaults` profile object, which should allow it to see all settings (saved or not!) that are present on that object.

It's just like this:

1. Set the default font size at 9
2. Go to a different profile page (already existent) and observe the font size to be 9!

wait what the heck is going on

## No saving
![11392-no-save](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18356694/136275503-54d515c5-f152-48db-9270-81e6776bb8c4.gif)


## with saving
![11392-with-save](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18356694/136275728-e506eb38-d124-4e49-a6df-266524ab589f.gif)

> 
> 
> @ianjoneill quick question, did you _save_ the settings before making the duplicate?
> 
> If I:
> 
>     1. Set your default font size to 9.
> 
>     2. Save the settings
> 
>     3. Make a duplicate of the "PowerShell" profile.
> 
> 
> Then the duplicate will have the font size set to 9.

My default font size is 9 - that's state that has existed since time immemorial on my machine.

If I duplicate the PowerShell profile from a brand new terminal instance (i.e. the terminal is loaded up with the defaults set with a font size of 9), I see the issue.

Stepping through the code, there's definitely something wrong.

If I stick this:

```cpp
                std::wstringstream ss;
                ss << L"Original size " << profile.FontInfo().FontSize() << L" Duplicated size " << duplicated.FontInfo().FontSize() << L"\n";
                OutputDebugStringW(ss.str().c_str());
```

before line 215 here:
https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/c727762602b8bd12e4a3a769053204d7e92b81c5/src/cascadia/TerminalSettingsEditor/MainPage.cpp#L215

I get `Original size 9 Duplicated size 12` printed out.

`TerminalSettings::CreateWithProfile()` doesn't look at the font size from the default settings, it gets it straight out of the profile - which has the size set to 12, so the terminal preview on the settings page shows the font size as 12.

https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/c727762602b8bd12e4a3a769053204d7e92b81c5/src/cascadia/TerminalSettingsModel/TerminalSettings.cpp#L65

review_comments: might be worth documenting _why_ not every caller needs it, for the future
